A wild herb flourishing in open fields, prized for its medicinal qualities. 

Its blossoms cluster, blooming and fading in a ceaseless dance. Because of this, many believe it holds the power to ward off death and restore life. 

In truth, people harvest only its withered petals, which leave behind a cool, lingering fragrance. 

The drier the air, the stronger the scent—a subtle reminder to desert travelers that someone, somewhere, still awaits their return.

4917127472894683828:
Qiuqiu wasn’t born from a mother Dog—it sprang out from the grass!
Perhaps because Qiuqiu always hung around the lawn, over time, passing Villagers started saying so.
But what do they know about the joy of rolling in the grass? With a freshly found Wild Fruits in its mouth, Qiuqiu peeked out from the grass like a fluffy flower blooming in the field.
When the sun set, Qiuqiu finally decided to come out. It bounced around, shaking off the grass seeds stuck all over its fur, leaving a trail of seeds in its paw prints.
The seeds fell, sprouted in spring, and Qinghe would once again wear a lush green coat next year.
